title: Bonifacio Ruggieri and Alfonso Rossetto (Este envoys in Rome) → Ercole II d'Este: letter on Bologna and Ferrara, the last third in cipher
correspondents: Bonifacio Ruggieri and Alfonso Rossetto → Ercole II d'Este, Duke of Ferrara
shelfmark: Uppsala universitetsbibliotek, Waller collection, Waller Ms it-01133
folio_note: 2 leaves (292 x 211 mm), 3 images: f. 1r has 18 lines of clear text then 10 lines of cipher; f. 1v opens with 4 more cipher lines, then the close and both signatures; f. 2v the address. About 14 lines, perhaps 550-650 signs.
status: Viewed 11 Nov 2026 (the three TIFFs, read at 1,000 px a page). Alvin record 192068: 'Matters concerning the relations between Bologna and Ferrara, partly written in cipher.' The cipher is a set of letter-like signs and letters with diacritics (b, d, x, y, t, l with strokes and loops), written continuously; nothing is written between the lines or in the margin, and no decipherment sheet is among the images. Dealer's stamp of Damiano Muoni: a stray from the Este envoys' correspondence, whose main run is in Modena. Not on DECODE.
why: Ferrara's envoys at the court of Paul III on the Bologna-Ferrara dispute; the clear part sets the subject, the cipher holds what they would not write openly.
score_note: Scored from the scans during the 11 Nov 2026 Nordic sweep (research/sweep_2026-11-11_nordic/); all three images viewed
verify: Transcribe the 14 lines at full size; look in Archivio di Stato di Modena, Cancelleria ducale, Ambasciatori, Roma (busta for 1543, Ruggieri) for sister letters with chancery decipherments and for the envoys' cifrario.

title: "Kloge Søren" (Søren Christensen): his Cyprianus, a book of charms and cures written almost wholly in a symbol cipher
correspondents: Søren Christensen, "Kloge Søren" (1843-1925), cunning man, writer and owner
shelfmark: Det Kgl. Bibliotek (Copenhagen), Dansk Folkemindesamling, DFS 1997/020 (Kloge Sørens samling, from Petra Mosegaard)
folio_note: 90 leaves in one octavo volume, 109 images online; about 85 written pages of roughly 12 lines, most of it cipher in red ink; six loose slips of formulas in a second, angular sign alphabet
status: Viewed 11 Nov 2026 (contact sheet of 12 openings across the book; opening 12-13 at 1,700 px). Running text in a sign alphabet of strokes, dots, hooks and bars, with no word spaces; headings partly in clear Danish ('for Kjertelsyge', 'mod Troldom hos Fjeder-Kræet', 'at faae een Tyv til at hensvinde som Duk for Solen', 'mod Hexerie og Forgjörelse hos Mennesker og Dyr', 'For Svindsot'), a SATOR square on p. 58. No key and no decipherment on the leaves or in the record. The library's description: 'Størstedelen i lønskrift' (most of it in secret writing). Not on DECODE.
why: A complete working handbook of a 19th-century Danish cunning man, with the cures hidden in his own cipher; the clear headings give the subject of every section.
score_note: Scored from the scans during the 11 Nov 2026 Nordic sweep (research/sweep_2026-11-11_nordic/); 13 openings viewed
verify: Ask Dansk Folkemindesamling whether a key or transcription is filed with Kloge Sørens samling; 'Det farlige Liv' (Nationalmuseet 1978, p. 77) reproduces a page of his astrological notes in the same kind of writing and was not opened (not online).
